title: Add modules/security-groups-baseline for Redwood Private (secure defaults + custom port validation)
author: Bruno Silva
description: Summary: Introduces a new Terraform module `modules/security-groups-baseline` that provisions a least-privilege set of security groups intended for Redwood Private (VPC) deployments. This is the default SG bundle used by the wrapper module (follow-up PR) and aligns with the installer’s networking assumptions (preflight checks expect specific reachability patterns). The module is secure-by-default (no 0.0.0.0/0 ingress; egress is restricted to VPC CIDRs by default with explicit toggles), and it includes input validation for any customer-provided custom ports and CIDRs. Motivation: We saw early pilot configs drift toward overly-permissive SG rules (especially “open admin” and broad east-west). This baseline reduces variance and support burden while still allowing controlled exceptions for enterprise networking (e.g., shared services, centralized egress, TGW). Scope: (1) Security groups and rules for Redwood Private component tiers: `control_plane`, `data_plane_workers`, `customer_admin_access` (optional), and `vpc_endpoints` (optional). (2) Explicit interfaces for allowed admin CIDRs, intra-VPC CIDRs, and optional shared-services CIDRs. (3) Validation: port numbers/ranges, CIDR formatting, and guardrails preventing known-unsafe combinations (e.g., enabling public admin ingress). (4) Outputs contract: stable names/IDs intended for `redwood-private-installer` wiring. Notes/assumptions: This module does not attempt to model NACLs (kept as guidance-only per Security thread); it assumes subnet tiering from `vpc-baseline` (public/private/isolated) but only requires VPC ID + CIDR inputs to function. Egress: default egress is limited to `allowed_egress_cidrs` (defaults to VPC CIDR) plus AWS prefix lists when endpoint mode is enabled. If a customer truly needs “allow all egress”, there is an explicit `allow_all_egress = true` escape hatch with a loud warning in README and a checkov skip justification template. Testing: `terraform fmt`, `terraform validate`, `tflint` (aws ruleset), and `checkov` are wired via the repo CI jobs. I also ran a local plan against the `examples/aws-private-alpha/minimal` stack with both `single_nat` and `per_az_nat` to ensure SG outputs line up with current module composition. Docs: README includes a port matrix, guidance for common enterprise constraints (no inbound from internet; admin via VPN/SSM; private-only endpoints), and a troubleshooting section for typical “installer can’t pull images” symptoms that are actually endpoint/egress misconfigurations.

feat(security-groups-baseline): add control plane SG + rules (api/health/intra-vpc)
feat(security-groups-baseline): add worker/data plane SG + east-west rules
feat(security-groups-baseline): optional admin access SG (VPN/bastion CIDRs only)
feat(security-groups-baseline): optional interface endpoint SG rules

ci(checkov): tune policies and document suppression guidance for explicit escape hatches
changed_areas_summary: New module under `modules/security-groups-baseline` with component-oriented SGs and opinionated defaults; repo CI updated to include the new module in the terraform-docs/readme consistency check and in checkov/tflint matrices.
illustrative_snippet: variables.tf: `variable "custom_ingress_ports" { description = "Additional TCP ports to allow from allowed_admin_cidrs to the control plane" type = list(number) default = [] validation { condition = alltrue([for p in var.custom_ingress_ports : p >= 1 && p <= 65535]) error_message = "custom_ingress_ports must be valid TCP port numbers (1-65535)." } }` and `variable "allowed_admin_cidrs" { type = list(string) default = [] validation { condition = alltrue([for c in var.allowed_admin_cidrs : can(cidrnetmask(c))]) error_message = "allowed_admin_cidrs must contain valid CIDR blocks." } }`
review_conversation: Marcus Lin (Security): The default egress rule still allows 0.0.0.0/0 in one place (worker SG). We can’t ship that as default, even for alpha. Please restrict to VPC CIDR(s) and make any broader egress an explicit opt-in with docs + justification.

Bruno Silva (Author): Good catch — that was inherited from the template. I’ve changed defaults to egress only to `allowed_egress_cidrs` (defaulting to VPC CIDR) and added `allow_all_egress` escape hatch + README warnings. checkov now stays green without suppressions by default.

Kevin Osei (Security): Please add validation to prevent `allow_all_egress=true` when `private_only_endpoints=true` is set (it’s contradictory and often indicates confusion). Also add a short troubleshooting note: missing ECR/S3 endpoints often surfaces as image pull failures; folks will try to open egress instead of fixing endpoints.

Bruno Silva (Author): Added guardrail: if private-only endpoints is enabled, we error when allow_all_egress is true. Also added troubleshooting section with ‘don’t open egress to fix endpoints’ guidance + links to the endpoints module docs (to be added in PR-244/245 docs follow-up).

Irene Choi (Infra): Naming: please align outputs to what Ethan/Benji said the installer expects. Specifically, expose distinct SG IDs for control plane and workers, and expose a consolidated map output for future composition (`security_group_ids = { control_plane = ..., workers = ... }`).

Bruno Silva (Author): Updated outputs: `control_plane_security_group_id`, `workers_security_group_id`, `admin_security_group_id` (optional), plus `security_group_ids` map. Also updated README examples to reference the stable outputs.

Ethan Park (Platform): Preflight expects control plane to be reachable from workers on 443 and health port within VPC CIDRs. Can we codify that without forcing a single port? The installer may change health port later.

Bruno Silva (Author): Added variables for `control_plane_api_port` (default 443) and `control_plane_health_port` (default 8081) with validation, and used those in SG rules. README calls out that the installer should set these explicitly if it diverges.

Benji Okafor (Platform): Please ensure no cyclical dependencies between SG rules when the module is used alongside `vpc-endpoints`. Also, we should avoid implicit references to subnets to keep the module composable with existing VPC mode.

Bruno Silva (Author): SG rules are only CIDR/SG-ID based; no subnet references. Endpoint SG is optional and only created if `create_vpc_endpoint_sg=true`. No cycle observed in plan; added a note in README about composing endpoint SG rules (ingress from workers/control plane).

Marcus Lin (Security): Approved once the README clearly states: no public ingress by default; admin access must be via customer VPN/bastion/SSM with explicit CIDRs; any exceptions must be documented. Also add a short ‘alpha exceptions’ section listing what we’re explicitly not enforcing (NACLs).
Bruno Silva (Author): Done. Added ‘Secure defaults’ and ‘Out of scope (alpha)’ sections. No NACL resources; only guidance.
Ethan Park (Platform): Approved (with note to keep ports in sync with installer defaults).
post_merge_notes: Follow-ups: (1) Wire this module into `modules/redwood-private-vpc` wrapper (ENG-4824 continuation in PR-250). (2) Confirm installer defaults for health port and document in the quickstart. (3) Add endpoint SG usage guidance once `modules/vpc-endpoints` doc is finalized.
